purpose: What wave 18 LEARNED while executing, kept apart from what it PREDICTED before executing. The frozen forecast is immutable; falsifications are recorded here so a reader at HEAD can tell the two apart without consulting git history.
rule_this_establishes: Frozen forecasts are immutable. Falsifications discovered during execution are recorded in a sibling execution-notes artifact, linked to the frozen forecast and the baseline commit.

baseline_observations.method: `classify_stack_tensor_on(relative_name, operator)` called directly against real safetensors headers. It has to be direct: `opplan::build` returns on the residual-topology refusal before reading any operand, so a hyper-connection checkpoint emits no UnclassifiedOperand for its HC tensors and that absence is structural silence, not evidence. Same move `k3_representable.rs` makes one stage down, for the same reason.
baseline_observations.fixture: scripts/hc_header_fixture_export.py fetches the shard headers over HTTP range requests; no payload is read. 130 tensors across three checkpoints, indexed families capped at two real members.

evidence: 0.self_attn.q_proj.weight -> AttnQ under Softmax and MlaQProj under Mla — operator awareness is live, not assumed

forecast_falsifications.prediction: 'no placement rule owns the hc_attn_*, hc_ffn_* and hc_head_* tensor groups' — one gap, one mechanism
forecast_falsifications.reason: Three stages, and the gap splits across two. `graph::build::classify_group` owns tensor-GROUP placement (failure: UnplacedGroup) and does block top-level hc_head_*. `plan` owns config semantics and physical SegmentTensor {name,dtype,shape,offset,len} — bytes, never meaning. `opplan::build` owns semantic role binding via the operator-aware classify_stack_tensor_on (failure: ClosureDefect::UnclassifiedOperand). The layer-level hc_attn_*/hc_ffn_* groups are ALREADY physically placed by the `layers` prefix; their unresolved plane is role classification, not placement.

forecast_falsifications.prediction: GLM-5.3-Flash's layer HC tensors should surface as UnclassifiedOperand today
forecast_falsifications.reason: opplan::build returns on the residual-topology refusal before any operand is read — its own comment says so. The general lesson, beside #415's: absence of a downstream defect does not imply downstream capability when an earlier refusal prevents the observation from being made.

forecast_falsifications.prediction: mtp.0 is a silent-omission trap; prove HC total-fate matching catches its 18 tensors
forecast_falsifications.reason: COMPONENT_EXTERNAL_NAMESPACES = ["mtp"] is checked BEFORE the group-pattern scan precisely because `mtp.layers` contains 'layers' and would otherwise merge a distinct sub-model into the primary DecoderStack. DeepSeek already reports `mtp` as one honestly-unplaced group (finding 72), and graph::tests::build already pins the whole family as unplaced. The correct invariant is the opposite: adding HC role recognition must NOT give any mtp.* tensor a primary-stack fate.

forecast_falsifications.prediction: DeepSeek-V4-Flash is wave 18's subject; it needs 'attn_norm/ffn_norm spellings' alongside HC placement
forecast_falsifications.result: false, and the understatement was large
forecast_falsifications.reason: DeepSeek's ENTIRE tensor dialect is foreign — attn.wq_a, attn.wq_b, attn.wkv, attn.wo_a, attn_norm, ffn.experts.N.w1. Measured overlap with the role vocabulary is exactly ONE operand on layer 0: ffn_norm.weight -> PostAttentionNorm. Adding HC roles would move DeepSeek from 'all unclassified' to 'nearly all unclassified', attributing nothing. The forecast centred DeepSeek because wave 17's arithmetic ORACLE came from DeepSeek's reference; that is the right source for arithmetic and the wrong specimen for addressability.

forecast_falsifications.result: nearly — two, and the second is pinned
forecast_falsifications.reason: GLM-5.3-Flash is FP8, so each mlp.*_proj carries a weight_scale_inv block-scale sidecar, and those three are unaddressed for reasons unrelated to residual topology. The baseline pins all NINE unclassified operands rather than the six, so a wave-18 rule loose enough to swallow a scale sidecar fails the assertion instead of passing a narrower one.

preserved_question: Unchanged from the frozen forecast: can a declared hyper-connection topology acquire complete executable carriage — semantic operand roles entering the normal closure — without collapsing the namespace, payload, or execution boundaries? Only the specimen changed, because the originally chosen one cannot isolate the variable.

re_aimed_subjects.moonshotai/Kimi-K3: TRANSFER WITNESS — ordinary operands classify, four generic HC gaps remain, pinned independently in plan::tests::k3_representable::KDA_LAYER_UNADDRESSED by a programme with no stake in making this abstraction look general
re_aimed_subjects.deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash: DIALECT-BLOCKED CONTROL — must stay blocked; a wave-18 change that appears to unblock it is a leak, not progress

acceptance_criterion: Wave 18 succeeds when GLM's six hyper-connection operands acquire semantic roles and enter the normal operand closure without changing the classification of its already-supported operands OR its three FP8 scale sidecars; the same generic HC role machinery reduces K3's independently-existing HC addressability gap without K3-shaped names appearing in wave 18's vocabulary; DeepSeek remains blocked by its separate base-dialect deficit; mtp remains external to the primary stack; and no payload-backed execution claim is promoted.
